overview: This is an amended complaint filed by GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. on September 17, 2026, in ITC Investigation 337-TA-1500 against Tower Semiconductor and its affiliates. GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower's semiconductor devices infringe six of GlobalFoundries' U.S. patents relating to RF and power management manufacturing process technologies. The complaint seeks a limited exclusion order, cease-and-desist orders, and a bond.

points.point: GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. is a Delaware corporation with principal place of business at 400 Stonebreak Road Ext., Malta, NY 12020, and is a leading American semiconductor manufacturer and major recipient of CHIPS and Science Act funding.
points.quote: Complainant GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. is a Delaware Corporation with a principal place of business at 400 Stonebreak Road Ext., Malta, NY 12020.

points.point: The respondents are Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (Israel), Tower Partners Semiconductor Ltd. (Japan), Tower Semiconductor Italy S.R.L. (Italy), Tower US Holdings Inc., Tower Semiconductor San Antonio Inc., Tower Semiconductor NPB Holdings Inc., Tower Semiconductor Newport Beach Inc., and Newport Fab LLC.
points.quote: Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (Israel); Tower Partners Semiconductor Co., Ltd. (Japan); Tower Semiconductor Italy S.R.L. (Italy); Tower US Holdings, Inc.; Tower Semiconductor San Antonio, Inc.; Tower Semiconductor NPB Holdings, Inc.

points.point: GlobalFoundries is a leading American semiconductor manufacturer with over 4,500 U.S. employees that originated from AMD's semiconductor manufacturing arm in 2009 and acquired IBM's microelectronics facilities in 2015, gaining approximately 16,000 IBM patents and applications.
points.quote: GlobalFoundries originated from the semiconductor manufacturing arm of another leading U.S. semiconductor company, Advanced Micro Devices, in 2009, and expanded globally through acquisition and organic investment.

points.point: GlobalFoundries has invested more than $15 billion in its Fab 8 facility in Malta, New York over the past decade and committed an additional $16 billion in U.S. investment as a major CHIPS Act recipient.
points.quote: GF has invested more than $15 billion in its Fab 8 facility over the last decade to support innovation and manufacturing capacity.

points.point: Tower Semiconductor generated little over $1.5 billion in 2025 revenue and has historically underinvested in R&D, spending less than $90 million annually and filing fewer than 15 patent applications annually while holding fewer than 350 granted patents globally.
points.quote: with a base of operations in Israel, and plants in Japan, Europe and the United States, Tower generated a little over $1.5 billion in 2025, and forecasts revenue will grow beyond $2 billion.

points.point: The '235 Patent relates to transistor devices with nickel silicide layers formulated to prevent degradation upon removal of overlying stress liners, using compositionally graded platinum-doped nickel silicide with increasing platinum content toward upper surfaces.
points.quote: nickel silicide layers have a platinum composition gradient increasing in platinum content toward the upper surfaces thereof

points.point: The '983 Patent relates to high-voltage semiconductor devices with lateral double-diffused transistors featuring self-aligned channel wells adjacent to gate edges to achieve low drain-to-source on-resistance and high breakdown voltage.
points.quote: For high performance LD transistors, low drain-to-source on-resistance (Rdson) is desired to minimize its power dissipation

points.point: The '425 Patent describes self-aligned liners formed on metal semiconductor alloy contacts using deposited transition metal that reacts with the contacts to form etch-resistant transition metal-metal semiconductor alloy liners.
points.quote: Metal semiconductor alloy contacts are provided on each of a source region and a drain region

points.point: The '546 Patent relates to formation of contacts in dielectric layers over semiconductor substrates with intermix regions at the interface of contact bottom portions and upper portions of the substrate.
points.quote: The '546 Patent relates to forming an intermix region at an interface of a bottom portion of a contact and an upper portion of a semiconductor substrate.

points.point: The '748 Patent relates to segmented guard-ring and chip edge seals with low-K dielectric material in middle of line and back end of line processing to prevent moisture ingress.
points.quote: provides segmented guard-ring and chip edge seals with low-K dielectric material in middle of line (MOL) and/or back end of the line (BEOL) processing

points.point: The '167 Patent relates to formation of contacts in dielectric layers over semiconductor substrates, specifically forming intermix regions at interfaces of contact bottom portions and upper portions of the substrate.
points.quote: The '167 Patent relates to forming an intermix region at an interface of a bottom portion of a contact and an upper portion of a semiconductor substrate.

points.point: GlobalFoundries asserts claims 1-9 of U.S. Patent No. 9,093,425 (the '425 Patent), valid and enforceable until expiration on February 11, 2034.
points.quote: claims 1-9 of the '425 Patent in this Investigation

points.point: GlobalFoundries asserts claims 1-7 and 8-14 of U.S. Patent No. 9,865,546 (the '546 Patent), valid and enforceable until expiration on July 3, 2035.
points.quote: claims 1-7 and 8-14 of the '546 Patent in this Investigation

points.point: GlobalFoundries asserts claims 1, 2-8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, and 16-18 of U.S. Patent No. 10,062,748 (the '748 Patent), valid and enforceable until expiration on February 27, 2037.
points.quote: claims 1-12, 14, and 16-18 of the '748 Patent in this Investigation

points.point: GlobalFoundries asserts claims 1-6 of U.S. Patent No. 10,707,167 (the '167 Patent), valid and enforceable until expiration on May 30, 2036.
points.quote: claims 1-6 of th e '167 Patent in this Investigation

points.point: The accused products include at least the Qorvo PAC22140 Evaluation Kit, the Denso DNSRR004 Blind Spot Monitor Sensor, and the Qorvo QM81026 RF Power Tracker, all containing Tower-manufactured semiconductor devices.
points.quote: the Qorvo PAC22140 Evaluation Kit, the Denso DNSRR004 Blind Spot Monitor Sensor, and the Qorvo QM81026 RF Power Tracker

points.point: Tower's accused semiconductor devices are manufactured using Tower's RF processes (including 65nm RF process), BCD processes (including TS18SOI process), SiGe and BiCMOS processes (including SBC18 process), and logic processes.
points.quote: semiconductor devices manufactured using Tower's RF, power management, BCD, logic, SiGe, and BiCMOS processes

points.point: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower-made devices infringing the '235 Patent include at least devices manufactured using Tower's RF processes, including the Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker, which infringes claims 1, 5-9, 10, 11, 12, and 15-19 of the '235 Patent.
points.quote: Tower-made Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker (the "'235 Representative Accused Product") infringes at least claims 1, 5-9, 10, 11, 12, and 15-19

points.point: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower-made devices infringing the '983 Patent include products manufactured using Tower's BCD processes, including the PA22BZ die in the Qorvo PAC22140 Evaluation Kit, which infringes claims 1-7, 8-12, 13-18, 19, and 20 of the '983 Patent.
points.quote: Tower-made PA22BZdie in the Qorvo PAC22140 Evaluation Kit (the "'983 Representative Accused Product") infringes at least claims 1-7, 8-12, 13-18, 19, and 20

points.point: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower-made devices infringing the '425 Patent include the M7DN25PS die in the DENSO DNSRR004 Blind Spot Monitor Sensor and the Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker, which infringe claims 1-9 of the '425 Patent.
points.quote: Tower-manufactured M7DN25PS die in the DENSO DNSRR004 Blind Spot Monitor Sensor and the Tower-made Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker (the "'425 Representative Accused Products") infringe at least claims 1-9

points.point: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower-made devices infringing the '546 Patent include the M7DN25PS die in the DENSO DNSRR004 Blind Spot Monitor Sensor and the Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker, which infringe claims 1-14 of the '546 Patent.
points.quote: Tower-made Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker (the "'546 Representative Accused Products") infringe at least claims 1-14

points.point: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower-made devices infringing the '748 Patent include products manufactured using Tower's BCD processes, including the PA22BZ die in the Qorvo PAC22140 Evaluation Kit, which infringes claims 1-12, 14, and 16-18 of the '748 Patent.
points.quote: Tower-made PA22BZdie in the Qorvo PAC22140 Evaluation Kit (the "'748 Representative Accused Product") infringes at least claims 1-12, 14, and 16-18

points.point: GlobalFoundries alleges that Tower-made devices infringing the '167 Patent include the M7DN25PS die in the DENSO DNSRR004 Blind Spot Monitor Sensor and the Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker, which infringe claims 1-6 of the '167 Patent.
points.quote: Tower-made Qorvo QM81026 Power Tracker (the "'167 Representative Accused Products") infringe at least claims 1-6

points.point: The Qorvo PAC22140EVK1 Evaluation Kit was purchased in the United States from Mouser Electronics on March 13, 2026, with import tariffs applied ($56.25), confirming importation into the United States.
points.quote: Exhibit 29 is a set of receipts showing the purchase of a Qorvo PAC22140EVK1 in the United States from Mouser Electronics on March 13, 2026.

points.point: The Qorvo QM81026 RF Power Tracker chip is a component of a smartphone assembled in India and imported into and sold in the United States, with purchase receipt from February 28, 2026.
points.quote: The Qorvo QM81026 RF Power Tracker chip ("Qorvo QM81026 RF chip") is a component of a smartphone, which is assembled in India and is imported into and sold in the United States.

points.point: The Toyota Blind Spot Monitor Sensor containing the Denso DNSRR004 rear and side radar sensor with Tower-manufactured MMIC was purchased in the United States from Jim Coleman Toyota in Maryland on October 13, 2025, with photographs indicating it was made in Japan.
points.quote: purchase of a Toyota Blind Spot Monitor Sensor in the United States from Jim Coleman Toyota in Maryland on October 13, 2025

points.point: GlobalFoundries satisfies the economic prong of the domestic industry requirement through its manufacturing in the United States since 2012 at facilities in Austin Texas (design center), Burlington Vermont (manufacturing center), Dallas Texas (design and engineering center), Malta New York (manufacturing center), Raleigh North Carolina (design center), and Santa Clara California (design center and customer support).
points.quote: GlobalFoundries has been manufacturing products in the United States since 2012, and it owns or leases numerous domestic facilities in the United States.

points.point: GlobalFoundries invests over $500 million annually in R&D and technology enablement and employs thousands of engineers to sustain its innovation leadership in RF and power management process technologies.
points.quote: GlobalFoundries invests over $500 million annually in R&D and technology enablement

points.point: The Asserted Patents are the subject of a civil action being concurrently filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas.
points.quote: The Asserted Patents are the subject of a civil action being concurrently filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas.

points.point: GlobalFoundries seeks a permanent limited exclusion order barring from entry into the United States infringing semiconductor devices, products containing same, and components thereof manufactured by or on behalf of, or imported by or on behalf of, Tower or its affiliates.
points.quote: Issue a permanent limited exclusion order under 19 U.S.C. § 1337(d)(1) barring from entry into the United States infringing certain semiconductor devices

points.point: GlobalFoundries seeks permanent cease and desist orders directing Tower Respondents to cease and desist from sale for importation, importation, sale after importation, distribution, offering for sale, promotion, marketing, advertising, testing, demonstration, warehousing, solicitation of sales, programming, repair, maintenance, use, transfer, and other commercial activity relating to infringing semiconductor devices.
points.quote: Issue permanent cease and desist orders, under 19 U.S.C. § 1337(f), directing the Tower Respondents to cease and desist from the sale for importation

points.point: GlobalFoundries seeks imposition of a bond upon the Proposed Respondents during the 60-day Presidential review period pursuant to 19 U.S.C. § 1337(j) on infringing articles imported during that period.
points.quote: Impose a bond upon the Proposed Respondents who continue to import infringing articles, including certain semiconductor devices, products containing same, and components thereof, during the 60-day Presidential review period

points.point: The investigation generally concerns semiconductor devices and methods of manufacturing semiconductor devices that incorporate the functionalities and technological advancements of the six asserted patents.
points.quote: This investigation generally concerns semiconductor devices and/or methods of manufacturing semiconductor devices.

points.point: The accused products category includes certain semiconductor devices manufactured using Tower's RF, power management, BCD, logic, SiGe, and BiCMOS processes, including wafers, chips, and components thereof.
points.quote: certain semiconductor devices manufactured using Tower's RF, power management, BCD, logic, SiGe, and BiCMOS processes, including wafers and chips
